files.title: Properties of Materials
files.description: Objects are made of different materials. Materials have properties like hard, soft, rough, smooth, shiny, and dull.

files.title: States of Matter
files.description: Matter can be a solid, a liquid, or a gas. Solids keep their shape. Liquids flow and take the shape of their container. Gases spread out to fill their space.

files.title: Changes of State
files.description: Heating and cooling can change matter from one state to another. Melting, freezing, evaporating, and condensing are all changes of state.

files.title: Light and Sound
files.description: Light travels in straight lines and can be blocked to make shadows. Sounds are vibrations that travel through air. We use light and sound to communicate.

files.title: Physical and Chemical Change
files.description: A physical change changes the size or shape of matter but not what it is made of. A chemical change creates a NEW substance with different properties.

files.title: Mixtures
files.description: A mixture is made by combining two or more materials. The materials in a mixture do not chemically change — they can often be separated again.

files.title: Force and Motion
files.description: A force is a push or a pull. Forces can make objects start moving, stop, or change direction. Mass and force both affect how objects move.

files.title: Magnets
files.description: Magnets attract iron and steel objects. Every magnet has two poles: North (N) and South (S). Opposite poles attract; same poles repel.

files.title: Classification of Living Things
files.description: Scientists sort living things into groups. All living things grow, need food, and reproduce. Animals are sorted by features like backbones, fur, feathers, or scales.

files.title: Animals
files.description: Animals grow and change through life cycles. Animals have body parts that help them survive. Some animals live in groups for protection and finding food.

files.title: Plants
files.description: Plants have parts like roots, stems, leaves, and flowers. They make new plants through seeds. Flowering plants have life cycles from seed to flower.

files.title: Traits and Adaptations
files.description: Traits are features of a living thing passed from parents to offspring. Adaptations are special traits that help an organism survive in its environment.

files.title: Earth's Features
files.description: Earth has land features like mountains, valleys, and plains. Water covers most of Earth as oceans, lakes, and rivers. Earth has many natural resources.

files.title: Earth Events
files.description: Earthquakes, volcanoes, and erosion can change Earth's surface. Some changes happen quickly, others happen very slowly over time.

files.title: Units and Measurement
files.description: We measure time in seconds, minutes, hours, and days. We measure distance in centimetres, metres, and kilometres. Mass is measured in grams and kilograms.

files.title: Materials in Objects
files.description: Objects are made of one or more materials. The materials chosen for an object depend on the properties needed — strength, flexibility, or waterproofing.

files.title: States of Matter
files.description: All matter is made of tiny particles. Solids have particles packed tightly in a fixed shape. Liquids flow and take the shape of their container. Gases spread to fill any space.

files.title: Phase Change
files.description: Phase changes occur when matter changes state. Heating adds energy causing melting and evaporation. Cooling removes energy causing condensation and freezing.

files.title: Heat and Thermal Energy
files.description: Thermal energy is the total energy of moving particles in matter. Heat flows from warmer objects to cooler ones. Temperature measures how hot or cold something is.

files.title: Physical and Chemical Change
files.description: Physical changes alter shape or state but not composition. Chemical changes create new substances with different properties. Evidence includes colour change, gas production, heat, or light.

files.title: Force and Motion
files.description: Forces can be balanced or unbalanced. Unbalanced forces cause objects to speed up, slow down, or change direction. Mass and force both affect motion.

files.title: Magnets
files.description: Magnets attract ferromagnetic materials. Magnetic force can attract or repel. Stronger magnets have greater magnetic force. Magnets can solve engineering problems.

files.title: Animals
files.description: Animals have life cycles, behaviours, and adaptations. Pollinators and seed dispersers help plants reproduce. Group behaviour provides survival benefits.

files.title: Plants
files.description: Plants make their own food through photosynthesis. They have specialised parts — roots, stems, leaves, and flowers. Flowering plants reproduce using seeds dispersed in many ways.

files.title: Ecosystems
files.description: An ecosystem is a community of living things and their environment. Food chains and webs show how energy moves from plants to animals. Every organism has a role.

files.title: Fossils
files.description: Fossils are remains or imprints of organisms from long ago, preserved in rock. Scientists study fossils to learn about ancient life and how organisms have changed over time.

files.title: Weather and Climate
files.description: Weather is the day-to-day condition of the atmosphere. Temperature is measured with thermometers. Climate is the typical weather pattern of a region over a long time.

files.title: Earth's Features & Water Cycle
files.description: The water cycle moves water between Earth's surface and atmosphere through evaporation, condensation, and precipitation. Earth has diverse land and water features.

files.title: Earth Events
files.description: Earth's surface is changed by earthquakes, volcanoes, erosion, and other events. Some changes are rapid, others occur over millions of years. Scientists classify changes as fast or slow.

files.title: Engineering Practices
files.description: Engineers identify problems and design solutions. They test, improve, and compare designs. Science knowledge about forces, materials, and the environment helps engineers solve real problems.

files.title: Units and Measurement
files.description: Scientists use standard units to measure time, distance, mass, and volume. Using standard units lets scientists share and compare measurements accurately.
